x: Jayavarma was a Brihatpalayana king whose capital was Koduru near Machilipatnam.

s: Which dynasty ruled the Andhra region immediately after the Ikshvakus, before the Salankayanas?
x: The order after the Ikshvakus was Brihatpalayanas, Salankayanas, Vishnukundins and then the Eastern Chalukyas.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Brihatpalayanas:
1. Jayavarma is their only known king.
2. Jayavarma is described as Maheshwara-pada-parigrahita.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Jayavarma is the only known Brihatpalayana king and is described as Brahmanical and Maheshwara-pada-parigrahita.

s: Which development led to the rise of the Vishnukundins?
o: The Salankayanas established a new empire in Telangana.
Samudragupta’s southern campaign weakened the Pallavas.
The Mauryas restored Ikshvaku rule in Vijayapuri.
The Pallavas strengthened their authority after defeating Samudragupta.
x: The Vishnukundins rose after Samudragupta’s southern campaign of 358 CE weakened the Pallavas.

s: Which was the capital of the Anandagotrika (Kandara) kings?
x: The Chejerla inscription places the Anandagotrika capital at Kandarapuram; Vengi was Salankayana and Vijayapuri Ikshvaku.

s: Who among the following Ananda Gotra kings issued the Mattepadu plates and patronised Buddhism?
x: Damodara Varma of the Anandagotrikas issued the Mattepadu plates and leaned to Buddhism ('meditating at the feet of Samyak-Sambuddha'); Atti Varma performed the Hiranyagarbha (Gorantla plates).

s: Which plates record the Hiranyagarbha danam performed by Atti Varma of the Ananda gotra?
x: The Gorantla plates record that Atti Varma (Attivarman) of the Ananda gotra performed Hiranyagarbha danam.

s: Which was the capital of the Ikshvakus?
x: Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda) was the Ikshvaku capital; Vengi was the Salankayana capital.

s: Which is regarded as the earliest copperplate grant in Andhra?
o: Chikkulla plates of Vikramendra Varma II
Ipur plates of Madhava Varma I
x: The Prakrit Kondamudi plates of the Brihatphalayana king Jayavarma, issued from Kuduru, are the earliest copperplate grant in Andhra.

s: Who was the founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty and a vassal of the Vakatakas?
x: Indravarma was the founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty and a vassal of the Vakatakas. He built Indrapalanagara.

s: For how many years did Madhava Varma I rule?
x: Madhava Varma I ruled for 22 years, married a Vakataka princess and is associated with the Undavalli, Bhairavakona and Mogalrajapuram caves.

s: Who was the last ruler of the Vishnukundin dynasty?
x: Manchana Bhattaraka was the last Vishnukundin ruler; Vikramendra Varma II issued the Chikkulla and Tundi plates and Indrabhattaraka is linked with Ghatikas.

s: Vikramendra Varma I was the son of Madhava Varma II by a princess of which dynasty?
x: Vikramendra Varma I was the son of Madhava Varma II by the Vakataka princess.

s:
Consider the following statements about Govinda Varma I:
1. He expanded into the Krishna-Godavari region.
2. He bore the title Shadabhigna.
3. He was the founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Govinda Varma I expanded into the Krishna-Godavari region and was called Shadabhigna; the founder was Indravarma.

s: Whose reign is regarded as the golden age of the Vishnukundins?
x: Madhava Varma II was the greatest Vishnukundin ruler; his reign is called the golden age and saw a Vedic revival.

s:
Arrange the following Vishnukundin rulers in chronological order:

a. Govinda Varma I

b. Indravarma

c. Madhava Varma II

d. Madhava Varma I
x: The order is Indravarma (founder), Madhava Varma I, Govinda Varma I and then Madhava Varma II.

s: A twelfth-century inscription from Bezawada preserves which legend about Madhava Varma II?
o: He sentenced his own son to death after the prince’s chariot killed a poor woman’s son.
He founded the Eastern Chalukya dynasty at Vengi.
He married his daughter to Ishanavarma of the Maukharis.
He abdicated after losing Vengi to the Salankayanas.
x: The Bezawada inscription narrates that Madhava Varma II sentenced his own son to death after the prince’s chariot killed the son of a poor woman.

s: Which combination correctly represents the sacrifices attributed to Madhava Varma II?
x: Madhava Varma II is credited with performing 11 Ashvamedhas, 16 Rajasuyas and one Purushamedha.

s: The Khanapur plates, found in Satara district of Maharashtra, record the marriage of Madhava Varma II with a daughter of which ruler?
o: Pulakeshin II of the Badami Chalukyas
x: The Khanapur plates record Madhava Varma II’s marriage with a daughter of Vakataka ruler Prithvisena II.

s: From which dynasty did Madhava Varma II take Karma-rashtra up to the Gundlakamma?
x: He took Karma-rashtra up to the Gundlakamma from the Pallavas; Vengi was taken from the Salankayanas.

s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title Satyasraya?
x: Indrabhattaraka Varma bore the title Satyasraya; Govinda Varma was Shadabhigna and Vikramendra Varma I was Mahakavi.

s: Madhava Varma II won the title Trikuta-Malayadhipati by defeating which rulers?
x: Madhava Varma II acquired the title Trikuta-Malayadhipati after defeating the Anandagotrikas. Trikuta was identified with Kotappakonda in Guntur.

s: In the title Trikuta-Malayadhipati of Madhava Varma II, which place does Trikuta refer to?
x: Trikuta is Kotappakonda in Guntur; the title came after he defeated the Anandagotrikas.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Shadabhigna was Govinda Varma's title; Mahakavi was Vikramendra I, Satyasraya Indrabhattaraka and Trikuta-Malayadhipati Madhava Varma II.

s: Which of the following titles was borne by Madhava Varma II?
x: Madhava Varma II bore the title Janasraya. Shadabhigna belonged to Govinda Varma, Mahakavi to Vikramendra Varma I, and Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya to Vikramendra Varma II.

s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title 'Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya'?
x: Sakala Bhuvana Rakshabharanaikashraya was a title of Vikramendra Varma II.

s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title 'Trisamudradhipati'?
x: Trisamudradhipati (lord of the three seas) was one of the titles of Madhava Varma II.

s: According to most historians, to which social group did the Vishnukundins belong?
o: Only hereditary feudatories of the Pallavas
x: Most historians regard the Vishnukundins as Brahmins belonging to the Vishnukundina gotra, although alternative caste theories have also been proposed.

s: Which region is indicated by the early records and forts as the original home of the Vishnukundins?
o: Telangana, including Amrabad, Keesaragutta and Indrapalanagara
The Krishna-Godavari coast after the Pallava wars
The coastal delta around Vengi alone
The southern Tamil region around Kandarapuram
x: Early records and forts at Amrabad, Keesaragutta and Indrapalanagara point to Telangana as the original home. The Vishnukundins later expanded into coastal Andhra.

s: Which of the following pairs on the origin of the Vishnukundins is correctly matched?
o: K. Gopalachari – Brahmins who adopted Kshatriya ways
x: B.V. Krishna Rao regarded the Vishnukundins as Brahmins. K. Gopalachari proposed an Agnikula Kshatriya origin and N. Venkataramanayya called them Brahmins who adopted Kshatriya ways.

s: Which historian held that the Vishnukundins were Agnikula Kshatriyas?
x: K. Gopalachari called them Agnikula Kshatriyas; B.V. Krishna Rao held they were Brahmins.

s: Keesaragutta may mark the beginning of the Vishnukundins as feudatories of which dynasty?
x: Keesaragutta may mark their start as Vakataka feudatories; the founder Indravarma was a Vakataka vassal.

s: With which place is the name of the Vishnukundin dynasty generally linked?
x: Historians generally take 'Vishnukundi' as the Sanskrit form of Vinukonda, a hill-fort town in the Guntur (now Palnadu) region.

s: With which place is Indrapalanagara, the early Vishnukundin capital, identified?
x: Indrapalanagara (Sukrapuram), built by Indravarma and the capital of Madhava Varma I and Govinda Varma, is Tummalagudem in Telangana.

s: Which of the following was regarded as the first capital of the Vishnukundins?
x: Amarapura was the first capital of the Vishnukundins. The rulers referred to themselves as Amarapurishulu.

s: After acquiring the Krishna region, the Vishnukundins used which place as a capital for some time?
x: Bezawada, or Vijayawada, was used as a capital for a period after the Vishnukundins acquired the Krishna region.

s: With which place is Amarapura, the first Vishnukundin capital, identified?
x: Amarapura is identified with Munnanuru in Amrabad, where yaga-vedikas were found; Tummalagudem was Indrapalanagara.

s: Which Vishnukundin ruler moved the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru?
x: Of these options Vikramendravarma is the one the APPSC G2 Mains 2025 final key accepted (it accepted Vikramendravarma and Madhavavarma). NextGen credits Madhava Varma II, who is not listed here; Vikramendravarma II's Chikkulla plates were issued from Denduluru.

s: Constant wars with which dynasty made the Vishnukundins shift their capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru?
x: Constant wars with the Pallavas led to the shift of the capital to Denduluru (credited in the APPSC key to Vikramendravarma, by some texts to Madhava Varma II).

s: Who built Indrapalanagara, the early capital of the Vishnukundins?
x: The Tummalagudem inscription says the founder Indravarma built Indrapalanagara.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Velpuru pillar is associated with Madhava Varma II, not Govinda Varma I. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which is regarded as the first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana?
x: The Tummalagudem plates, associated with Govinda Varma I, are regarded as the first Sanskrit inscription found in Telangana.

s: In which language was Govinda Varma's Chaitanyapuri inscription written?
x: Of the 21 Vishnukundin inscriptions, Govinda Varma's Chaitanyapuri record was in Prakrit, so not all were in Sanskrit.

s: To which ruler do the Chikkulla plates, containing the Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul', belong?
x: The Chikkulla plates (Tuni, East Godavari) are of Vikramendra Varma II and carry the Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul'.

s: To which ruler do the Ipur plates, bearing Lakshmi and conch symbols, belong?
x: The two Ipur plates from Tenali belong to Madhava Varma I.

s: What do the Polamuru plates of the Vishnukundins describe?
o: A marriage with a Vakataka princess
A grant to a Buddhist vihara
x: The Polamuru plates (Ramachandrapuram) describe divine ordeals; the Vakataka marriage is in the Khanapur plates.

s: Of the 21 known Vishnukundin inscriptions, how many are copper-plate records?
x: The 21 inscriptions comprise 16 copper-plate and 5 stone records.

s: Which Vishnukundin ruler issued the Tummalagudem plates granting land to Paramabhattarika's vihara?
x: The Tummalagudem plates of Govinda Varma I record the grant to his queen Paramabhattarika's vihara.

s:
Match the following:

List-I (Inscription)
a. Ramatirtham plates
b. Tummalagudem plates
c. Khanapur plates
d. Chikkulla plates

List-II (Ruler)
1. Madhava Varma II
2. Vikramendra Varma II
3. Indravarma
4. Govinda Varma I

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Ramatirtham - Indravarma; Tummalagudem - Govinda Varma I; Khanapur - Madhava Varma II; Chikkulla - Vikramendra Varma II.

s: The Vishnukundins formed a link between which two phases of Andhra history?
o: The Pallava age and the Maukhari age
The Satavahana age and the Ikshvaku age
The Ikshvaku age and the Eastern Chalukyas
The Gupta age and the Kushana age
x: The Vishnukundins link the Ikshvaku age with the Eastern Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukyas took over their agrahara system and administration.

s: Which Maukhari king defeated the Vishnukundin ruler Indrabhattaraka Varma?
x: Indrabhattaraka Varma was defeated by Maukhari Ishanavarma and was killed in the Kalinga war.

s: In which year did Pulakeshin II defeat Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala (Kolleru), ending Vishnukundin rule?
x: Pulakeshin II ended Vishnukundin rule at Kunala near Kolleru in 624 CE; his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana then founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.

s: Who founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi after the fall of the Vishnukundins?
x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana, brother of Pulakeshin II, founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.

s: Indrabhattaraka Varma was killed in the Kalinga war by Prithvimula of which dynasty?
x: Prithvimula of the Ranadurjayas, with a Kalinga king, killed Indrabhattaraka Varma.

s: The Jaunpur inscription records the marriage of Indrabhattaraka Varma's daughter to a prince of which dynasty?
x: Maukhari Ishanavarma defeated Indrabhattaraka, and his son married Indrabhattaraka's daughter (Jaunpur inscription).

s: Who defeated Manchana Bhattaraka and ended the rule of the Vishnukundins?
x: The Badami Chalukya Pulakeshin II defeated Manchana Bhattaraka at Kunala (Kolleru) in 624 CE.

s: Where did Pulakeshin II defeat the last Vishnukundin ruler Manchana Bhattaraka?
x: The battle that ended Vishnukundin rule in 624 CE was fought at Kunala, near Kolleru lake.
